DICOM RT Structure Set · public LCTSC data

RTSTRUCT Anatomy

How one structure set file is put together: what nests inside what, how it points to its CT, how the per-ROI lists join up, and how flat lists of numbers become organ outlines. Every value on this page comes from the real file.

1 · The map

How the pieces connect

Boxes inside boxes are sequences inside sequences. Click any box to find it in the file browser below. Hover an ROI row to see it line up across the three lists.

2 · The code

Reading it with pydicom

Recipes in the order you'd learn them. Every snippet ran against this file when the page was built, and Out is its real output. Like notebook cells they share variables, starting from path (the RTSTRUCT file) and ct_folder (the folder with its CT).

API at a glance
3 · The file

Every element, with its pydicom path

The full tree, as pydicom reads it. Sequences with more than 5 items show the first 2. Click a line to see its tag, data type, meaning, and the exact code to reach it.

4 · The geometry

From ContourData to outlines

Each polygon is one ContourSequence item: a flat list x₁,y₁,z₁, x₂,y₂,z₂ … in mm (patient coordinates, LPS). Move through the slices, then click an outline to see its points and the code that reads it. Polygons of one ROI on one slice combine by the even-odd rule, so a polygon inside another is a hole.

Data: patient LCTSC-Train-S1-001, physicians' structure set, values shown unmodified. LCTSC (Lung CT Segmentation Challenge 2017), The Cancer Imaging Archive, DOI 10.7937/K9/TCIA.2017.3R3FVZ08, licensed CC BY 3.0.
